doc.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023

title: Why American films record in London and crediting musicians
summary: No residuals on UK film recording and quick orchestras attract American productions; musician credits are becoming standard.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Am I correct that American film producers and directors often come to London to record partly because it’s more economically feasible for them?

That is a part of it because there are no residuals on film recording in the U.K. So the big — I mean it’s a double-edged thing. They think that the orchestras are better in London and quicker, their reading is quicker, their interpretation is quicker. But also there are no residuals so that becomes a big thing in their thinking.
Is it common in England for English films for the musicians to get credit in the scroll?

It’s starting to happen. It’s happening a lot now — I think it’s become a mandatory thing in American movies, to credit the musicians. In my experience there are directors who I’ve worked with who insist on crediting people, and there are who don’t. I mean I’ve just done a film, I think everybody’s credited. I haven’t seen it yet but I suspect everyone has been credited.
